findings.message: This is an instance fix, and it repeats the class that was already reported as a blocker in hr/contracts.ts. When there is no viewer, `mayAllocate` now trusts `ctx.actor.kind === "system"`. That is a structural field on a plain object, and any code path that builds a ServiceContext literal can set it. The diff's own test builds such a literal by hand (`{ tenantId: T, actor: { id: "sp:x", kind: "service" }, ... } as never`). Changing `"service"` to `"system"` turns that same literal into an unscoped writer. This is also a second copy of the 'is this a trusted system context' rule (B4): hr decides trust for `contextFor.job` contexts itself, and the two checks can disagree. Fix: use the single unforgeable system-context check that core/hr uses for `contextFor.job` (a brand or registry check, not a field check). Add a variant that proves a hand-built `{ actor: { kind: "system" } }` literal is refused.
findings.scenario: allocate({ tenantId: T, actor: { id: "x", kind: "system" }, source: "api", principal: {} } as never, { person: "LL-0417", projectKey: "CON", month: "2027-05", percent: 100 }) → the write succeeds with no project-scope check, when it should be refused as forbidden.

findings.message: This is a class miss of last round's B3 finding. The grid now reports `hidden`, but the newly scoped contract reads do not. `visible()` silently drops the rows of people the reader can't see, so `listAllocations` and `personMonthTotals` return `[]` both for 'this person has no allocations' and for 'you may not see this person'. A consuming module can't tell these apart and will read a hidden person as 0% allocated, or as on the bench. Fix: return the hidden person ids or a count with the result (for example `{ rows, hidden }`), or throw or flag when requested `personIds` fall outside the scope. Cover this with a variant test over Leadership, AU-limited HR, and an explicit out-of-scope `personIds` request.
findings.scenario: personMonthTotals(tx, auOnlyHrViewer, { from: "2026-12-01", to: "2026-12-01", personIds: [ayesha.id] }) → [], which is the same result as for an unallocated person. The new scope.test.ts asserts this ambiguous result as correct (rows: 0).

findings.message: `span()` counts months with its own year/month string arithmetic, next to `monthsBetween`/`nextMonth`, which already walk the same range. The cap check and the write loop can drift apart. Derive the cap from one month helper, for example by counting with the same `nextMonth` walk or a shared months.ts helper.
The name `team_` for the system job context next to the `team` parameter is easy to misread. Rename it, for example to `sys` as the tests do.

`hidden` is computed as `ids.length - people.length` and the screen labels every one of those people 'outside your HR access'. Any id with allocations that `listPeople` does not return for another reason (a person row that was removed, or a filter on status) is also counted. A Leadership viewer would then be told people are outside their access. Fix: count hidden people against the same ids read with the system context, and count missing hr rows separately.
findings.scenario: An allocation row whose person_id has no hr.person row, viewed by Leadership with everyone=true → hidden=1, and the UI says '1 more person is outside your HR access'.

findings.message: The previous finding said `copyMonth` inherits the missing-viewer bypass through its `allowed` filter. The fail-closed table only drives `allocate`. No case runs `copyMonth` with a service-kind context that has no viewer, so the second caller is not checked to refuse rather than quietly copy nothing. Fix: add copyMonth rows to the same table, for a no-viewer service principal, a system job and a PM.
findings.scenario: copyMonth({ actor: { kind: 'service' }, no viewer }) might return a successful 'copied 0' instead of forbidden, and no test would catch it.
